reason: E1 shows that deformation-induced defects delay void coalescence in a related alloy, supporting one premise, but neither E1 nor E2 addresses the central claim that reducing constituent count in Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni systematically lowers stacking fault energy or increases defect density relative to the quinary baseline. E2 demonstrates transformation-induced plasticity in a different alloy system (VCrFeCoNi) and does not provide evidence for the proposed composition–stacking fault energy relationship in the Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni family.
premises: Reduced constituent count lowers stacking fault energy or alters phase stability in Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni subsets
Lower stacking fault energy promotes deformation-induced twinning and martensitic transformation
Deformation-induced defects (twins, martensite) delay void nucleation and coalescence
Quaternary/ternary alloys will show higher defect densities than the equiatomic quinary under high-rate/cryogenic loading
Higher defect densities enhance work hardening and strength-ductility balance
